body.statement: Let \(L^{\mathrm{pkg}}=\mathsf E_{\mathrm{pkg}}^{0.1.0}(G,Z)\) be the labels externally returned by \(\texttt{szonszein/interference}\) version \(0.1.0\), function \(\texttt{make\_exposure\_map\_full\_neighborhood}\), and let \(L^{\mathrm{ref}}=\mathsf E_{\mathrm{ref}}(B,Z)\) be independently recomputed. If \(G\) is the disjoint union of the unequal clique components \(B_1,\ldots,B_L\), then \[L^{\mathrm{pkg}}=L^{\mathrm{ref}}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad A_l+C_l=1\text{ for every }l.\] In particular, because the pinned package map labels its second column by the complement of All Treat, a mixed block produces an explicit second-column mismatch with the target All Control map. On a valid clique input, \(\Phi(G,B,D,\alpha,L^{\mathrm{pkg}},L^{\mathrm{ref}})\) returns \(\texttt{label-equal}\) and the exact \(q_l=2^{-r_l}\), observed unanimous-block statistics, \(S\), \(M\), \(\omega_\alpha\), \(\rho_\alpha\), and \(I_{\mathrm{HT},\alpha}(D)\) exactly when the displayed equality holds; otherwise it returns \(\texttt{label-mismatch}\) with a coordinate witness and no interval. If any \(N_G[i]\ne B_l\) for \(i\in B_l\), including overlapping-neighborhood or nonclique inputs, it instead returns \(\texttt{graph-reject}\) with a structural witness before performing the label equality check and produces no interval.
body.justification: The proposition makes the software claim a reproducible equality test against a pinned implementation and separates graph-domain rejection from assignment-dependent label disagreement.
body.gap: AronowEcklesSamiiZonszein2021 demonstrates the \(R\) exposure workflow, but its companion package interface does not certify that the returned two-column labels equal the target unanimous All Treat and All Control map on each realized assignment.
body.consumer: A package user receives either a certified exact rare-exposure interval, a concrete package-versus-reference coordinate mismatch, or a distinct structural rejection for an overlapping or nonclique graph.
